newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela proposed '98 budget sees 5.5 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela proposed '98 budget sees 5.5 pct growth.

text.p: Venezuela's proposed 1998 budget, forecasts economic growth rising to 5.5 percent from an estimated five percent in 1997, a copy of the 11.24 trillion bolivar ($23.2 billion) budget showed.

The budget, which still has to be approved by Congress, also foresees the fiscal surplus falling to 1.34 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) versus an estimated 1.7 percent this year, even as spending falls in real terms by 9.8 percent.
Debt service payments are seen rising to 23.1 percent of total spending, at 2.6 trillion bolivars, of which 85.2 percent is due on external debt.
Venezuela begins amortization of its $17 billion restructured Brady debt this year. Total debt service payments this year are seen at 22.7 percent of total spending, the document showed.

On the revenue side, the budget foresees oil receipts falling in real terms by two percent of gross domestic product and accounting for 37.7 percent of total spending compared to 42.7 percent in 1997.
Taxes, on the other hand, are seen rising to 5.4 trillion bolivars, or 47.85 percent of the budget, compared to 3.8 trillion bolivars or 37 percent of the budget this year.
The proposed budget, which was due to be presented to Congress today, was delayed after Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar excused himself for health reasons.
A new date is yet to be set. Congressional approval is required before November, otherwise the 1997 budget will be rolled over into 1998, as happened last year.
